left_shoulder.why: Shoulder height sets the base of the shot; if it moves, the release point moves with it.

drills.name: Wall shoulder slides
drills.howto: Back against a wall, slide the arms up and down keeping the shoulders level and down.

drills.name: Mirror set-point holds
drills.howto: In front of a mirror, lift into the set point and hold, checking both shoulders stay level.
drills.cue: Lift the ball, not the shoulders.

right_shoulder.why: A level guide-side shoulder keeps the ball travelling straight to the rim.

drills.name: Wall shoulder slides
drills.howto: Back against a wall, slide the arms up and down keeping the shoulders level and down.

left_elbow.why: The shooting elbow drives the ball up; its path decides the arc and the line of the shot.

drills.name: One-hand form shooting
drills.howto: Close to the rim, shoot with the shooting hand only, elbow under the ball, and hold the finish.
drills.cue: Elbow under the ball, finish tall.

drills.name: Elbow-up lift
drills.howto: From the pocket, lift the ball straight up to the set point without shooting, then reset.

right_elbow.why: The guide-hand elbow should stay relaxed so it doesn't push the ball off line.

drills.name: Guide-hand off shots
drills.howto: Shoot form shots and lift the guide hand off the ball just before release.

left_wrist.why: The shooting wrist is the last thing on the ball; its height and timing set the release.

drills.name: Lying-down release
drills.howto: On your back, shoot the ball straight up so it lands back in your hands.
drills.cue: Snap the wrist, fingers to the sky.

drills.name: Freeze-the-finish
drills.howto: Shoot from close range and hold the follow-through until the ball lands.
drills.cue: Hand in the cookie jar until it drops.

right_wrist.why: The guide hand should leave the ball cleanly; a late or low guide wrist can push the shot.

drills.name: Guide-hand off shots
drills.howto: Shoot form shots and lift the guide hand off the ball just before release.
